The substitution of hydrogen by the nitro (-NO2) group in alkane/other hydrocarbons is called nitration. This reaction is carried out in presence of fuming of concentrated nitric acid or in presence of high temperature i.e at 400- 5000 C with alkanes. The major products are nitroalkanes.
In these reactions, alkanes are heated with concentrated sulphuric acid. Fuming occurs.
The fuming of SO3, it dissolves in conc. H2SO4 and sulphonic acid is obtained by the
substitution of one hydrogen atom by sulphonic group (-SO3H).

2. Oxidation of ethane a. Combustion Due to the highly combustible nature of alkanes they burn readily in the presence of oxygen. So alkanes are used as good fuels in different forms, like LPGs. It shows that the reaction is exothermic. When alkanes are burnt in the presence of oxygen, carbondioxide and water are formed with an excess amount of energy.
Note: Generally, in the combustion of hydrocarbons, mainly energy is released and byproducts are carbon dioxide and water.
b. Catalytic oxidation 2CH4 + O2 𝐶𝑢, 100 𝑎𝑡𝑚 /∆ → 2CH3OH CH4 + O2 𝑀𝑜𝑂, 200𝑎𝑡𝑚 /∆ → HCHO + H2O
As you have seen above, alkanes give aldehydes and alcohols at catalytic oxidation.
